c.tagline: One of Islam's holiest cities, wrapped in a UNESCO-listed medina

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but drivers sometimes push for a flat negotiated fare with tourists; insist on the meter or agree a price beforehand

emergency.note: Response times can be slower than in coastal tourist areas; larger hotels can help coordinate assistance

avoid.reason: In the medina expect persistent carpet-shop touts and 'the museum is closed' style steering scams; keep valuables secure in crowded souks.

hood_desc: Kairouan's UNESCO-listed walled old city, home to the Great Mosque of Kairouan (Mosque of Uqba), one of the oldest and holiest mosques in the Islamic world. Maze-like souks sell the city's famous carpets and leather goods, and the whole quarter is ringed by 9th-century ramparts.

Named for the Zaouia of Sidi Sahbi, the ornately tiled 'Barber's Mosque' shrine to a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, this quarter draws pilgrims from across North Africa. It's quieter than the central medina but equally rich in Islamic architecture.

The area around the Bab Tunis gate on the medina's edge, a busy transition zone where traditional souks meet modern shops and transport hubs. It's a practical, workaday district good for local shopping and catching louages to other towns.

A modern strip on the edge of town built up with mid-range hotels catering to day-trippers visiting on tours from the coast. It lacks historic character but offers more comfort and easier parking than the medina.

The French colonial-era 'new town,' laid out with wider boulevards, the train station, and administrative buildings. It's more orderly and less atmospheric than the medina but useful for banks, pharmacies, and transport.

water.note: Officially treated but most visitors and many locals stick to bottled water.

transit.hours: Roughly 6am-8pm for local buses and louages; limited service after dark
transit.pay: Cash only, paid on board or at the louage station
transit.map: No official app; louage stations are organized by destination near the medina edge
transit.note: Most of the medina itself is only navigable on foot; louages are the practical way to reach other Tunisian cities

train: SNCFT regional rail connects Kairouan to Tunis and Sousse
bus: SNTRI intercity buses run from Tunis, Sousse, and other coastal cities

tip.r: Around 10% at sit-down restaurants is appreciated; small change for guides at the Great Mosque and taxi/louage drivers is customary
